text:
maria.chen: Heads up — my Node SDK streaming tests started failing from my laptop (on corp network) with "UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY" when connecting to api.redwood.com. Non-streaming requests work fine. Node v18.16, undici 5.x.

maria.chen: Quick log snippet: 
```
Error: unable to get local issuer certificate
    at TLSSocket.onConnectSecure (_tls_wrap.js:1513:34)
    at TLSSocket.emit (events.js:526:28)
```

maria.chen: I tried NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/corp-ca.pem and pointing https.Agent ca to fs.readFileSync('/etc/corp-ca.pem') but still seeing the error for streaming. Any ideas?

sam.keller: Did you check whether the corporate proxy is terminating TLS and re-signing? If so you need the corp CA in the trust chain for the TLS client.

maria.chen: Yes it's the corp proxy. Surprisingly curl to the same endpoint works for me when I pass --cacert /etc/corp-ca.pem. So I think cert is fine. Only Node streaming path fails.

alex.gray: Streaming often uses HTTP/1.1 keepalive + chunked + different socket reuse. Some libraries open raw sockets and bypass the usual Node TLS options. Which client are you using for streaming? undici or native https?

maria.chen: undici's Pool/Stream API (we use client.stream()).

sam.keller: undici has its own Agent and can be sensitive to how you pass the ca. Make sure you're creating the Agent with ca and passing that Agent into the client. Example: 
```js
const { Agent } = require('undici');
const agent = new Agent({ tls: { ca: fs.readFileSync('/etc/corp-ca.pem') } });
const client = new Pool('https://api.redwood.com', { dispatcher: agent });
```

sam.keller: Also check NODE_OPTIONS and whether any global OpenSSL config is different on your laptop.

max.li: Another gotcha: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS works for the core TLS stack but if undici is linked against a different OpenSSL or uses a separate TLS binding it might not pick that up. Passing ca explicitly is safer.

jenna.martin: FWIW we had a case where the corp proxy inserted an intermediate cert and the server chain returned by proxy included duplicate certs which confused the verifier during streaming socket reuse. Running openssl s_client helped. Try: 
```bash
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -showcerts -CAfile /etc/corp-ca.pem
```
Check for any "unable to get issuer" lines and the cert chain order.

maria.chen: Good point — I ran s_client and saw two certs with same subject in the chain (proxy issuer + real issuer). Could that be it?

alex.gray: Yes duplicated or out-of-order chain can break validation on certain code paths. If the proxy sends an extra cert that duplicates the CA it can confuse the verifier. We solved it by using a cleaned CA bundle: concat only the corp root and pass that as ca.

maria.chen: After trimming the bundle to just the corp root and using undici Agent tls.ca it started working. Thanks! :tada:

devops-bot: Note: corp-proxy cert rotation planned 2024-10-15 02:00 UTC. If you rely on system stores, expect brief failures.

sam.keller: For reproducibility, add a note in the SDK docs about undici streaming + corp proxies: prefer explicit Agent with tls.ca or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS fallback, and a troubleshooting checklist (openssl s_client, check for duplicate certs).

maria.chen: Will open a small PR to docs and add a short example for troubleshooting. cc @alex.gray for review.

alex.gray: Happy to review, ping me in the PR. :thumbsup:
